name: manual_a10088
claim: GNU coreutils flock(1) (the standalone command) is not present on macOS/BSD by default -- confirmed missing even on a fully-set-up dev machine, not just a fresh install. Never gate a bash script's mutual-exclusion on the flock command; use Python's fcntl.flock() instead (a real POSIX syscall wrapper available in Python's stdlib on Darwin) if the script already shells out to python3, or the portable mkdir-is-atomic lock idiom if it's pure bash.

decisions.notes: Wrote 'exec 9>lockfile; flock 9' in a new bash+python provider-swap script, following the pattern I assumed was portable. Confirmed via 'command -v flock' that it's simply absent on this macOS machine -- would have failed for every user of the script, not just an edge case. This exact gotcha was already documented elsewhere in this same codebase (exa-mcp-wrapper.sh's own comments) but I didn't check for it before writing new locking code, so I nearly reintroduced a bug the codebase had already solved once.
